rawCandidates.selectionReason: Booking-search hero model for fast service/date/location decisions.
Best pet-adjacent decision flow for choosing care type, cadence, and duration.
Shows broad care-category discovery without starting with a fake groomer photo.
Three-step process section maps to intake, coat/service fit, and appointment prep.
Service rows with duration/price/action logic for full groom, puppy intro, de-shed, and nails.
Warm family-confidence plan comparison adapts to anxious pet-owner decisions.
Plain service-menu anatomy with book actions and business details.
Soft category cards and review tile show how photo temptation can be restrained.
Provider profile proof structure is useful for verified response/service facts.
Single-offer booking page with sticky pricing rail and service details.
Centered booking card is useful for one constrained appointment offer.
Booked/price visual overlays suggest safe proof artifacts without copying claims.
Pet-specific flow state with selected care option, time, duration, and next CTA.
Pet-care date/time flow helps distinguish recurring/longer care from quick visits.
Pet-type selection warns against ecommerce density while inspiring pet-specific choice tokens.
Generic service-card page is useful as an anti-reference.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Make the page help owners choose the right visit: full groom, puppy intro, de-shed, or nail trim.
Start with pet need and visit type before explaining the grooming menu.
Use large selectable service tiles with label, short description, and next-step CTA.
Selecting a pet need should reveal the safest next booking or enquiry path without a full app flow.

bannedUses: Do not copy Care.com caregiver marketplace positioning, puns, address collection wording, or care categories that Cedar Paw does not offer.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Turn services into clear rows: full groom, puppy intro, de-shed, nail trim, each with a plain reason to choose it.
Each row needs a book/enquire action so the owner does not have to return to the hero.
Route complex coat/puppy cases to a short fit question instead of pretending availability is known.
Rows need readable labels, visible focus, and touch-sized book buttons.

bannedUses: Do not invent prices, ratings, reviews, salon names, staff names, pet photos, or exact Fresha category language.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Collapse the pet-need selector into a vertical mobile flow with one strong next button.
Service, cadence, time, duration, selected, disabled, and empty states must be explicit.
Use Seattle-local time, US phone/address formatting, and service-duration language only when verified.
Do not expose address or private pet details until the owner has chosen a real booking/contact path.

bannedUses: Do not copy dog-walking labels, confirmed-caregiver privacy copy, address values, or recurring-care promises.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: When reviews/photos are unavailable, use process proof: intake, coat check, groom plan, pickup instructions.
Write calmly for anxious pet owners: practical, specific, and safety-conscious without medical or certification claims.
Give each process step enough room so safety guidance feels deliberate, not buried.
Use grooming-object or step icons only as support, never as fake pet outcomes.

bannedUses: Do not copy healthcare/provider copy, treatment timelines, doctor portraits, medication graphics, or guaranteed outcomes.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Use a warm, confident headline scale that feels careful rather than cute or frantic.
Warm neutral surfaces can create trust while avoiding cartoon pet colors and all-green sameness.
A soft assessment band can hold the first action without making the whole page a stack of cards.
Use low, controlled depth around the chooser only; avoid heavy shadows on every section.

bannedUses: Do not copy legal-plan language, family asset claims, plan pricing, or financial product structure.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: If real pet/grooming photos are missing, use restrained service artifacts and approved placeholders rather than cute stock pets.
Icons should clarify coat care, puppy intro, de-shed, nails, timing, and location only.
Use gentle but stable radii for pet-friendly warmth; avoid toy-like bubbles everywhere.
Prefer static lightweight imagery or CSS service markers until owner-supplied photos are approved.

bannedUses: Do not copy medical-product imagery, review graphics, supplement claims, or Hims/Hers brand styling.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Pair a plain service explanation column with a persistent booking/enquiry rail for the chosen visit.
If motion is used, keep it to selected-service transitions or rail updates, not decorative pet animations.
Tokenize one action color, neutral surfaces, row spacing, focus rings, and service tile sizes.
Expose service names, location, and contact path as visible and agent-readable facts.

bannedUses: Do not copy freelancer marketplace UI, sidebar nav, hourly/fixed pricing labels, skills chips, or profile identity.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Support package comparison without overwhelming the immediate booking decision.
Only use response time, ratings, reviews, certifications, or package counts if Cedar Paw provides source proof.
Group service packages by owner decision rather than internal grooming jargon.
Package cards must remain scannable and operable when stacked on mobile.

bannedUses: Do not copy Fiverr badges, pro labels, review counts, response-time claims, package prices, or marketplace contact menus.

antiReferences.rejectionReason: Generic AI service-card layout would make the pet grooming page feel template-made and unspecific.
Dense ecommerce navigation and pet-product personalization are wrong for a local appointment page.
Cute stock-cat shop imagery is a warning against photo-led pet cuteness when owner-approved grooming photos are unavailable.
B2B metric claims and floating SaaS cards would create fake proof and the wrong business tone.

remixDirection.summary: A calm pet-grooming booking page that starts with the owner decision, uses service-fit tiles and service rows, replaces cute stock-photo temptation with grooming-process artifacts, and keeps proof strictly source-backed.
selectedMoves: Care.com-style pet need selector adapted to grooming visit choice, not marketplace care matching.
Fresha/Square service-row clarity for full groom, puppy intro, de-shed, and nail trim actions.
Hims process-card restraint translated into grooming intake, coat check, groom plan, and pickup prep.
Origin warm assessment tone for anxious owner confidence without legal/financial claims.
Contra-style booking rail for the chosen service, rebuilt as a local grooming enquiry/booking module.
explicitRejects: No invented dog photos, before-after images, groomer names, review counts, safety certifications, prices, or veterinary claims.
No marketplace appointment counts, ecommerce pet-product navigation, SaaS metrics, or generic AI service cards.
No exact layout copy from any shortlisted Mobbin screen.
